body.rationale: Governing IPS status: ratified, as stated in the task; the header ips_status field was not shown, so any faculty sign-off outstanding is unconfirmed. Hard breaches are therefore real. I ranked on covariance-based reasoning and IPS fit, in line with the paper's late-cycle finding. 1) risk_parity: the CRO score is 0.41 and the only breach is volatility at 7.56%, a small miss that a blend can fix. It spreads risk across 14.3 effective assets and takes no return forecast. Reviewers flagged that effective N measures capital rather than risk dispersion, and that the Sharpe is CMA-based. Both are framing faults, not execution errors. 2) tail_risk_parity: it is similar and covariance-only, with volatility 7.67% as the sole breach and a drawdown of -20.9%. Its weakness is that semicovariance uses about half of all months, not the tail. 3) inverse_volatility: it has no IPS breaches, a clean forecast-free construction and effective N of 14.8. Its blind spot is about 43% in correlated credit and sovereign sleeves, and the drawdown of -22.9% is within the limit. 4) cvar_minimization: it has no breaches, the best backtest Sharpe at 0.74 and a drawdown of -18.7%. I ranked it lower because it is concentrated (2.9 effective assets in 4 names) and its 8.00% volatility was tuned to the floor, as its reviewer noted. 5) black_litterman: it has no breaches and a drawdown of -21.9%, and it adds return-optimized diversity to the ensemble. Reviewers criticised its equilibrium prior because ETF AUM double-counts overlapping equity sleeves, and it depends on stock-bond hedging holding. My first choice beats my fifth because risk_parity needs no return view or contaminated prior and its single, small volatility breach is easier to repair. Black-Litterman clears the IPS but leans on a distorted prior and a stable negative stock-bond correlation, which is the weak point of its drawdown headroom. I left out resampled_efficient_frontier because its drawdown of -24.84% is 16bp inside the limit, so compliance is fragile. I flag market_cap_weight: it has a backtest drawdown of -40.6%, which is 15.6 points beyond the limit. Its CRO score of 0.80 is the worst in the field. Reviewers also showed that its ETF AUM weights are not a market portfolio and double-count US large cap. It calls itself a diagnostic. I did not flag the adversarial diversifier, since orthogonality is valuable in an ensemble.
